item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-5ab6ce418229e78d","start_unit":125,"end_unit":126,"fact_summary":"Mexico's real GDP grew 3.2% in 2023, while official multidimensional poverty fell from 43.2% in 2016 to 36.3% in 2022, lifting 5.4 million people out of poverty. However, access to health worsened and the educational gap also deteriorated somewhat; the World Bank identifies persistent challenges in productivity, crime and violence, informality, infrastructure, public services, finance, competition, and regulatory uncertainty.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The source reports 2023 GDP and poverty outcomes through 2022, with the poverty trend providing context for the 2023 period; it does not isolate AMLO's causal contribution.","ruler_attribution":"National outcomes during AMLO's 2023 presidency; attribution is limited because the source is an economy-wide assessment and does not identify which policies or actors caused the changes.","limitations":["Poverty data are for 2022 rather than 2023.","The source does not provide program-level budgets, implementation records, appointments, or causal attribution to AMLO.","Crime, violence, productivity, informality, and service-access claims are presented as structural challenges rather than quantified 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5ab6ce418229e78d","start_unit":125,"end_unit":126,"fact_summary":"Mexico retained macroeconomic stability supported by an independent central bank and sound financial sector, but public-finance pressures increased because of greater state participation in growth, expanded social programs, efforts to improve public-service access and quality, infrastructure needs, and fiscal support to PEMEX; the World Bank says medium-term revenue reforms are needed to preserve debt sustainability.","question_ids":["5B.2","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment covers conditions relevant to 2023 and the medium-term fiscal outlook.","ruler_attribution":"The spending and state-participation choices occurred under AMLO's administration, but the source does not assign personal responsibility or evaluate specific decisions.","limitations":["No detailed figures are supplied for individual social programs, PEMEX support, infrastructure projects, or revenue reforms.","The source does not assess whether AMLO appointed or removed economic professionals based on competence or loyalty."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5ab6ce418229e78d","start_unit":126,"end_unit":126,"fact_summary":"Mexico's overall fiscal deficit was 4.3% of GDP in 2023, with revenues at 22.2% of GDP, public debt at 46.8% of GDP, and a primary deficit of 1.0% of GDP. Gross fixed investment grew 18.0% and government consumption 2.1%, while GDP growth was 3.2%.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The indicators are explicitly reported for calendar year 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These are national fiscal and economic outcomes during AMLO's administration; the source does not establish that the president personally directed each expenditure or outcome.","limitations":["The source does not evaluate spending quality, procurement, distributional incidence, or whether investment projects were completed effectively.","GDP and fiscal outcomes cannot by themselves establish program effectiveness or causation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5ab6ce418229e78d","start_unit":125,"end_unit":126,"fact_summary":"The World Bank identifies uncertainty around Mexico's ongoing constitutional reforms and judicial reform as a potential drag on investment, and notes that rating agencies were monitoring the associated fiscal and political risks.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.10","5B.4","5B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source discusses reforms underway during 2024, reflecting institutional and policy conditions emerging from the 2023 administration; it is not a direct 2023 outcome measure.","ruler_attribution":"The reforms were associated with the governing administration, but the supplied units do not specify AMLO's individual proposals, formal acts, or implementation record.","limitations":["The source does not describe the content of the reforms or establish whether they were enacted in 2023.","It does not document effects on courts, election bodies, legislatures, media, or oversight institutions."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied document is a World Bank macroeconomic outlook covering many countries; only units 125-126 concern Mexico.","No supplied units provide material evidence on nuclear risk, international peace, domestic violence, personal integrity, media freedom, appointments, corruption, or detailed social-program administration for AMLO in 2023."]}
